title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a heading or cover sheet (archive folio 57) for the following pages, 'Questions sur V.A. et groupes formels'. It names two topics, both tied to the May 1966 letter to Tate on crystals and Dieudonné theory.

(1) Barsotti's isogeny question. Let k be algebraically closed of characteristic p>0. Take abelian varieties A, B that are 'hypersingular' (Manin's term: no points of order p, i.e. p-rank 0). Suppose their formal groups (equivalently their p-divisible groups) are isogenous. Must A and B be isogenous? In dimension 1 this is Deuring's theorem: all supersingular elliptic curves over an algebraically closed field are isogenous. In dimension 2, p-rank 0 is the same as supersingular, with Dieudonné–Manin isogeny type G_{1,1}+G_{1,1}. So the question becomes: is a supersingular abelian surface isogenous to E×E with E supersingular?

(2) Realisability of p-divisible groups by abelian varieties over a fixed, non-algebraically-closed field k. One cannot in general embed (realise) a given p-divisible formal group as the p-divisible group of an abelian variety defined over k. The natural reason, implicit in a Tate-letter context: over a finite field, Frobenius on A[p^∞] has a characteristic polynomial with rational integer coefficients, given by Weil numbers. An arbitrary p-divisible group over k carries an arbitrary p-adic Frobenius, for instance an étale group Q_p/Z_p twisted by a transcendental p-adic unit. Such a group cannot occur, unlike over an algebraically closed field, where every symmetric Newton polygon is realised (Manin's conjecture).
errors: No mathematical errors on this page; it only states two questions. One terminological caveat: 'hypersingular' (p-rank 0) coincides with supersingular only in dimension at most 2. For g at least 3 the Barsotti question as posed with p-rank 0 is false: p-rank-0 varieties can have different Newton polygons, but then their formal groups are not isogenous, so the hypothesis already forces equal Newton polygons. The correct general statement is for supersingular varieties.

ideas.what: Do isogenous formal groups imply isogenous supersingular abelian varieties over an algebraically closed field? Equivalently, is every supersingular abelian variety isogenous to a power of a supersingular elliptic curve?
ideas.modern_name: Supersingular abelian varieties are isogenous to E^g (and for g at least 2 even isomorphic to E1×...×Eg)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deuring (g=1); Oort 1974-75, using Tate's theorem; Shioda for surfaces; Barsotti and Manin posed the question
ideas.where_published: Possibly mentioned in the Tate letter (May 1966) or in Montréal 1970 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné'; not certain

ideas.what: Not every p-divisible group over a non-algebraically-closed k comes from an abelian variety over k
ideas.modern_name: Realisation problem for p-divisible groups / Honda–Tate integrality constraints on Frobenius
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; Tate 1966, Honda 1968; over an algebraically closed field the realisation of Newton polygons is due to Manin's conjecture, proved by Serre and Oort

deep.surprise_reason: This is a title page listing two well-known questions from the mid-1960s, both later resolved or standard: Oort on supersingular varieties, and Honda–Tate theory. It only documents Grothendieck's awareness of them around the Tate letter.
transcription_corrections: The transcription is essentially correct. The struck-out word after 'Barsotti;' is likely 'et' (deleted). 'V.A.' means variété abélienne. The '57' at the bottom is the archive folio number.
